sections.h2: Where do I search property records in Polk County?
sections.html:
The Polk County Clerk of Courts keeps the Official Records, and its Public Records Searches page at polkclerkfl.gov links three separate searches. Official Records covers deeds, mortgages, marriage licenses, liens and HOA deed restrictions, and you can print uncertified copies from home for free.

The other two searches are court records and tax deeds. The court search covers civil cases, criminal cases and traffic tickets, along with dockets and filed documents. The tax deed search lets you look up tax deeds by tax number, parcel number or sale date, and the list of lands available for taxes sits in the same place.

Tax bills are handled by the Polk County Tax Collector at polktaxes.com, whose home page lists property taxes among its services. Use the clerk for what is recorded and the tax collector for what is owed.

sections.h2: What does Polk County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Polk is a big inland county: 2,011 square miles in total, with 1,798 of land and 213 of water. The county's profile calls it Florida's fourth largest county and notes that it is larger than Rhode Island. The county's 2023 profile cites a population of 787,404 from the 2022 Census.

There are 17 municipalities. Lakeland is the largest and Winter Haven is second, followed by Auburndale, Bartow, Davenport, Dundee, Eagle Lake, Fort Meade, Frostproof, Haines City, Highland Park, Hillcrest Heights, Lake Alfred, Lake Hamilton, Lake Wales, Mulberry and Polk City. The county has six traditional colleges and universities, including Florida Polytechnic University, with more than 19,000 students combined.

Because the county is so large, a house can be a long drive from the courthouse in Bartow. The online Official Records search matters here, since a title search can be done without a trip. One clerk records for every city and every unincorporated area.

sections.h2: What does recording a document cost in Polk County?
sections.html:
The clerk prints $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page of an instrument up to 14 by 8.5 inches. Indexing an instrument with more than four names adds $1.00 per additional name.

The table lists other charges the clerk prints on its fee page, which says the Florida Legislature regulates court fees, not the clerk's office.

The clerk accepts cash, credit card, money order or check, and adds a service charge on credit cards. A veteran's certificate of discharge is recorded without cost to the veteran.

sections.h2: How much is the deed stamp tax in Polk County?
sections.html:
It is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, the rate the clerk lists as in effect from August 1, 1992 to the present. The clerk's fee page also prints earlier rates, from 10 cents per $100 for November 1931 to June 1957 through 60 cents per $100 for June 1991 to July 1992, which helps when you read an old deed.

The Florida Department of Revenue says all parties to a deed are liable for the tax, whichever party agrees to pay. Consideration includes a mortgage the buyer takes subject to, whether or not assumed. Taxable instruments include warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds, a contract for deed and a deed in lieu of foreclosure. A spousal homestead deed where the only consideration is a mortgage is exempt, and so is a divorce deed for the marital home.

Section 689.01 requires a deed to be in writing and signed in front of two witnesses. Ask your closing agent to confirm the witnessing before the document goes to the clerk.

sections.h2: Which Polk County court fees matter to a distressed owner?
sections.html:
Owners facing foreclosure, an inherited house or a problem tenant will meet other clerk charges. The clerk prints $70.00 for holding a judicial sale and recording the certificate of sale and title, with another $70.00 for an electronic sale.

  • Removal of a tenant, county civil: $185.00.
  • Opening an estate: $231.00. Summary administration is $235.00 for estates under $1,000 and $345.00 at $1,000 or more. Formal administration is $400.00.
  • Starting a real property action: $400.00 under $50,000 of property value, $905.00 from $50,000 to $250,000, and $1,905.00 over $250,000, each needing a written estimate of value.
  • Release of a lis pendens: $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each subsequent page.

The Florida estate tax was eliminated for people who died after December 31, 2004, and personal representatives have not needed to file Form DR-312 or DR-313 since July 1, 2023. Summary administration under state law is available if the nonexempt estate does not exceed $150,000, or the decedent has been dead more than two years.

sections.h2: What should I check in the Polk County records before I sell?
sections.html:
Search the owner's name and the property description, and read every recorded item against the property. A buyer's title company will do the same search, so it helps to see the results first.

  • Mortgages with no recorded release.
  • Liens and judgments filed against the owner.
  • HOA deed restrictions, which the Official Records search covers.
  • Any tax deed or tax certificate activity, using the tax deed search.

A sale is a change of ownership for property tax, so the assessment resets to market value on the next January 1, with exceptions such as a transfer between spouses. Tell your buyer to expect a bill built on the sale value, and ask the Polk property appraiser or tax collector for the current figures on your parcel.

faqs.q: Who is the recorder in Polk County?
faqs.a: The Polk County Clerk of Courts. The clerk's Official Records search covers deeds, mortgages, liens, marriage licenses and HOA deed restrictions.

faqs.q: Can I print Polk County records for free?
faqs.a: Yes, uncertified copies from the Official Records, court records and tax deed searches can be printed at home for free. Certified copies cost $2.00 for the certification.

faqs.q: What is the first page recording fee in Polk County?
faqs.a: The clerk prints $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page. Instruments with more than four names add $1.00 per additional name.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp tax rate in Polk County?
faqs.a: It is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and the clerk lists that rate as in effect from August 1, 1992. All parties to the deed are liable for it.
